Age is the first thing worth knowing here and the answer is 1951, with 86.9 percent of the 4,795 units in Archer Heights finished before 1970 and 37.1 percent before 1940. Median size is 5.4 rooms, and rooms are what an interior quote is really counting.

Owner households here number 2,901 and renter households 1,606, a 64.4 percent owner-occupied place. The stock behind those households is 48.6 percent detached, 1.7 percent attached and 49.8 percent multi-unit, at a median of 5.4 rooms. The Census puts the median home value at $280,513.

Archer Heights is in the top four of the 22 Chicago community areas covered here for the largest share built before 1970 (86.9 percent), the smallest housing stock overall (4,795 units) and the smallest owner-occupied market (2,901 households). It is also near the top for the smallest homes by room count (5.4 rooms).

Set against the other places covered here, Archer Heights is furthest from the middle on three things: prewar housing at 37.1 percent against a 15.8 percent average, townhomes and rowhouses at 1.7 percent against a 7.5 percent average and housing in buildings of two or more at 49.8 percent against a 29 percent average.

Source: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, Community Data Snapshots 2026, drawing on American Community Survey 2024 estimates. Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

Why two houses in Archer Heights do not price the same

Masonry walls change the exterior job completely. On 37.1 percent prewar stock and a 1951 median, there is very little painted wall outside: the work is the porch, the cornice, the soffit, the fascia, the garage surround and the sash. All of it is detail, most of it is off a ladder, and none of it is quotable from a photograph. 49.8 percent of the housing sits in buildings of two units or more, which means hallways, stairwells and unit turnarounds are as much of the work as living rooms. Those get quoted per unit and they get done to a date.

What should be on a written quote in Archer Heights

  • Distance, stated. Archer Heights is 6.3 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Archer Heights is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.
  • Containment, not just paint. 86.9 percent of housing in Archer Heights was built before 1970, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.
  • Plaster as well as drywall. 37.1 percent of Archer Heights is prewar. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so wall repair is a different line from wall painting.
  • Setup does not shrink with the room. The median unit here is 5.4 rooms. Masking, cutting in and cleanup cost the same in a small room as a large one, so a flat per-room rate is usually wrong in one direction or the other.

Lead-safe work on Archer Heights houses

86.9 percent of housing units were built before 1970, and the community-area data does not publish a 1978 bucket, so the real pre-1978 share is higher than that by an amount nobody has measured in Archer Heights. Anything built before 1978 sits inside the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule the moment work disturbs its paint. Illinois never took the program on, so the agency behind it here is EPA itself.

What it changes is the front and the back of an Archer Heights job, not the middle: plastic and sealed openings before, a specific cleanup standard after. It starts at roughly six square feet of disturbed paint per room inside, twenty square feet outside, and always on window replacement.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Archer Heights.

The useful question is not whether the rule applies to your Archer Heights house. At 86.9 percent pre-1970 it very likely does. The useful question is what the containment and the cleanup are actually going to look like in your rooms, and it is a fair one to ask anybody.

Certification is a document, not a sentence on a website. It shows as pending below because no number has been supplied. Ask to see it, in Archer Heights and everywhere else.

Questions

Asked about Archer Heights

My house in Archer Heights is plaster, not drywall. Is that a problem?

It is not a problem, it is a different repair. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so the fix has to address the movement rather than the line. With a 1951 median build year most of Archer Heights is plaster over lath on at least some walls and ceilings. Say so when you call, because it changes the time estimate and it is better said before the quote than after.

How quickly can somebody look at it?

Archer Heights is 6.3 straight-line miles from the shop, which is close enough that looking at the work and doing the work do not have to be the same trip. That matters most on small jobs, because a repair that is worth doing gets seen instead of being pushed into a bigger job later. Call 708-935-4289.

Is the $280,513 median home value in Archer Heights what a job here costs?

No, and the two are unrelated. $280,513 is the Census estimate of what homes in Archer Heights are worth, and it is on this page because the age and the size of the housing describe the work. No price for painting or remodeling appears anywhere on this site, because no local range has been established that would survive being checked. Every job is quoted after we stand in it.

Who actually shows up in Archer Heights?
